question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed shared durable recovery authority and its new `durable` configuration/state contract before reviewing this cumulative implementation slice for landing?
rationale: The branch creates a new cross-owner runtime authority, persists coordination state in shared SQLite, and adds operator controls; repository policy reserves these compatibility and architecture choices for maintainer intent rather than contributor implementation alone.

options.title: Defer implementation until the stack gate
options.body: Keep this PR open but pause landing review until maintainers accept or narrow the RFC and shared-storage contract in the predecessor stack.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed owner-first slice
options.body: Approve only a named minimal recovery invariant and require the branch to remove unsupported modes, schema/versioning, and owners outside that scope.

options.title: Reject shared durable authority
options.body: Decline the cross-owner layer and request narrowly owner-specific recovery improvements through existing task, flow, subagent, and session APIs.

recommendation.title: Defer implementation until the stack gate
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but pause landing review until maintainers accept or narrow the RFC and shared-storage contract in the predecessor stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The related RFC names mjnkao as the contributor-side implementation owner and this PR’s series author; upstream acceptance still requires a repository maintainer.
